title: How Does Cashless Health Insurance Work in India?
content:
Cashless insurance removes the hassles of having to pay cash at the hospitals at the time of need. For cashless medical insurance, insurance providers enter into direct negotiations with hospitals in their network to pay for the treatment availed by the insured person. They tie up with some specific hospitals, known as the network hospitals of the insurance company.
When the insured gets hospitalised in a network hospital, they do not have to settle the bill with the hospital at the time of discharge. Instead, the TPA (third party administrator) or the insurance company will coordinate and settle the bill directly at the hospital.

title: Claim Cashless Health Insurance During Emergencies
content:
Medical emergencies come unannounced. To avail of cashless hospitalisation during such circumstances, follow the steps below:
Once the insured is admitted to the hospital, they must show a health card issued by the insurance company. The Health card will have all the vital details such as the insurer's name, policy number, plan type, etc.
Insured needs to contact the TPA/insurance desk and initiate the cashless claim by filling up a pre-authorisation request, usually within 24 hours of hospitalisation.
A third-party administrator/insurance company will review all the initial documents submitted.
Once the insurance company approves the cashless request, further documents are to be produced by the hospital to expedite the claim process.
Once the final set of documents submitted by the hospital is verified, the claim amount will be directly settled with the network hospital.
If admission to the specified list of network hospitals is not feasible, there is an option of a reimbursement claim. In this case, the insured would pay the bill in full, and they can file a claim with relevant documents and medical bills later on with the insurance provider.

title: What is an Individual Health Insurance Plan?
content:
Individual medical insurance is a type of health insurance plan that covers a single person under one policy. Unlike family floater plans, which share a sum insured among all insured members, individual medical insurance offers dedicated coverage solely for the person insured, ensuring better risk management and adequate financial protection.

title: 2. Waiting Period
content:
Next, the health insurance company checks the holding tenure of your health plan. There are many reasons why your insurer does so. For instance, critical ailments such as heart diseases, cancer, kidney failure, etc. have a ‘holding/ waiting period’. This waiting period could range anywhere between one year and four years, depending on the ailment. The insurance benefit for such aliments only kicks in once this waiting period has been successfully completed without an insurance claim.
The insurer will also go on to seek the primary diagnosis to understand the reasons for hospitalization. They determine if there are any new health developments and not a pre-existing condition that has been kept hidden/falsified to the insurer. If it is found that the hospitalization is due to an existing and undeclared health condition, then the insurer can refuse to provide any coverage and render the health insurance policy void.This will also make it difficult for you to get another health insurance coverage anywhere in India.

Things to remember before buying an individual health insurance plan in India
1. Estimate your Health Insurance Coverage
Although there are no fixed guidelines regarding the coverage one should have, there are certain parameters to keep in mind that will impact your health insurance needs.
Primarily, your age and income levels determine your premium. This is followed by factoring in your family history and pre-existing conditions. Another thing to remember is that if you have a predisposition to certain ailments, you should consider getting extra coverage. Similarly, you also need to factor in your geographical location as the standard of living and healthcare expenses in metro cities is much higher when compared to smaller cities.
2. Keep an Eye Out for Sub-limits on the Policy
Most health insurance plans do not cover all expenses incurred in case of an emergency. A sub-limit caps the reimbursement under various cost heads and is listed in the policy wordings of your health plan. For example, your room rent or ICU charges may be capped at 1% or 2% of the total sum assured. This means that despite having adequate insurance, you may still have to pay certain expenses out of your own pocket.
None of us would want to compromise on the care we may end up needing. Hence, be careful and understand all sub-limits when going through the proposed policy document.

title: Cashless Claim Process
content:

- Notify the Insurer: Inform the insurance provider about your admission within 48 hours. You will need to settle all bills directly with the hospital during your stay.

title: How Does a Family Floater Health Insurance Work?
content:
A Family Floater Health Insurance Plan operates under a single, shared policy that covers your entire family - typically you, your spouse, and your dependent children.
Here is how the coverage and mechanics work in practice:
Shared Sum Insured: Rather than each member having an individual limit, everyone shares one total financial pool (e.g. INR 10 Lakhs).Flexible Claims Usage: Any single family member can use the full sum insured in a policy year for a major illness, or multiple members can make separate claims until the shared limit is exhausted.Single Premium Payment: You pay one consolidated annual premium for the whole family, which is significantly cheaper than buying separate policies for each person.Automatic Reset (Restore Benefit): Many modern floater plans offer a restoration feature - if one member uses up the entire sum insured during a claim, the coverage limit automatically resets for subsequent claims by other family members (or for unrelated illnesses) within the same year.Age-Based Pricing: The premium is calculated based on the age of the eldest member included in the policy.Annual Renewal and Entry/Exit: You can easily add a newborn child or remove a member upon reaching adulthood during annual renewals.
answer_text:
A Family Floater Health Insurance Plan operates under a single, shared policy that covers your entire family - typically you, your spouse, and your dependent children.
Here is how the coverage and mechanics work in practice:
Shared Sum Insured: Rather than each member having an individual limit, everyone shares one total financial pool (e.g. INR 10 Lakhs).Flexible Claims Usage: Any single family member can use the full sum insured in a policy year for a major illness, or multiple members can make separate claims until the shared limit is exhausted.Single Premium Payment: You pay one consolidated annual premium for the whole family, which is significantly cheaper than buying separate policies for each person.Automatic Reset (Restore Benefit): Many modern floater plans offer a restoration feature - if one member uses up the entire sum insured during a claim, the coverage limit automatically resets for subsequent claims by other family members (or for unrelated illnesses) within the same year.Age-Based Pricing: The premium is calculated based on the age of the eldest member included in the policy.Annual Renewal and Entry/Exit: You can easily add a newborn child or remove a member upon reaching adulthood during annual renewals.

title: How does family floater health insurance work?
content: In a family floater medical insurance plan, the entire sum assured is shared among the family members, including an individual, spouse, dependent children, and parents. title: What is Hospital Cash Benefit?
content:
Hospital cash benefit is a daily lump sum amount the insured can get in case of hospitalization. It is either a part of the base plan or can be purchased as a rider or an option.
In most cases, the hospital cash benefit is only applicable if the insured has been hospitalized for a minimum of 48 hours. The hospital cash benefit is provided for every 24 hours completed during the time of hospitalization for 30-45 days in total under a policy year.
This amount can be used to cover additional expenses during hospitalization, such as , transportation, hiring a caregiver, etc., or to compensate for the loss of income during this time.

title: How Does a 10 Lakh Health Insurance Plan Operate?
content:

Any expenses not covered by the policy, such as deductibles or copayments, are the responsibility of the policyholder.Claim Process: For non-network hospital visits, the insured must pay expenses upfront and then seek reimbursement from the insurer by submitting original bills, documents, and a claim form. The insurer evaluates the claim and settles eligible expenses accordingly.

Therefore, to protect one's savings in a medical emergency, health insurance companies grant a period of grace to make the necessary payments.

title: Why Do You Need Health Insurance ?
content: Beyond saving on medical expenses, there are multiple reasons why you should get insured. In fact, it is advisable that you buy a policy while you are still healthy and young. The sooner you opt for a health insurance policy the better, as premiums and exclusions increase with age. Here are four reasons why you should consider buying a health insurance policy for yourself and your family. 1) Increase in lifestyle-related illnesses Although the human lifespan has grown over the years, stress levels have grown in parallel. Due to advancements in the field of medicine, people may live longer, but lifestyle-related habits can severely impact the quality of this ‘long’ life. Many people choose to live a sedentary lifestyle and opt for unhealthy meals to go with it. Pair this lifestyle with chronic stress and you have a recipe for early onset of conditions like hypertension and diabetes , which may lead to critical illnesses like stroke , heart attack and more. By choosing health insurance, one is choosing to mitigate the financial impact of being diagnosed with this kind of lifestyle ailment. 2) Group Health Cover is Usually Insufficient According to a survey by Big Decisions, about 95% of Indians today are not sufficiently insured, with individuals above the age of 45 in the highest risk group. Many rely on their group health plan to cover their medical costs. However, a group plan may not cover your entire family’s medical expenses. Additionally, the total sum insured you get through a group plan most likely will not be sufficient to meet all your medical expenses. Do not put yourself at risk of being underinsured by relying solely on group health coverage. Opt for a comprehensive health insurance policy instead. 3) You Are Covered for More than Just Hospitalization Health insurance provides coverage beyond your hospitalization costs. It covers medical bills, doctor’s consultations, ambulance charges, and more. Nowadays, there are pre and post-hospitalization expenses that are covered by traditional health insurance. This means you are getting more bang for your buck when you choose to invest in a comprehensive health insurance policy. 4) Inflation is leading to Out of Pocket Expenses Increasing Not only is the cost of living on the rise, but healthcare expenses are likely to be sky-high in the next ten years. India’s healthcare industry is experiencing inflation in the double digits. Your out-of-pocket expenses are likely to grow over the years unless you have financial measures in place to mitigate the impact of inflation. One such measure is investing in a health insurance policy. Health insurance can fortify you with the emergency finances necessary if you are ever in need due to unforeseen medical emergencies.

title: What is the eligibility criteria for health insurance?
content: The two main aspects that are considered when determining eligibility for health insurance are your age and current health. The minimum age to get health insurance for your child is 15 days, going all the way up to 18 years. For adults, the entry age is 18 years, and the maximum limit is 65 years. Your premium heavily depends on your age. It is lesser when you are younger; hence, experts advise that people should get health insurance as soon as they are financially independent, i.e. in their early 20s. The second factor is your overall health. When you buy health insurance, there are chances that you may be asked to undergo a medical examination to determine your current health status. Normally, this is reserved for people above the age of 45. If you are under 45, you may just be asked to present a doctor’s certificate claiming a proof of good health. However, people of all ages are required to declare pre-existing conditions, if they have any. These can include diabetes, hypertension, asthma, high blood pressure, thyroid, etc. Having a pre-existing condition does not mean that you are not eligible for health insurance. You most definitely are. This information is important to identify the best suited plan and coverage for the customer. It is imperative that you tell your provider of your pre-existing conditions to streamline the process when you make a claim and to avoid falling under non-disclosure.

title: Save Tax in India with Health Insurance Plans
content: Health insurance comes with a dual benefit for any policyholder. You secure your health while reducing your tax liability . With health insurance, you can claim a considerable amount as tax-deductible premiums paid toward your health insurance policy in a single year under Section 80D of the Income Tax Act . In several scenarios, you are entitled to a variety of tax deductions thanks to your health insurance policy. There are as follows: Scenario 1- Maximum tax deduction of INR 50,000/year Securing yourself, your spouse, and your dependent children with a health insurance policy, you can claim upto INR 25,000 annually as tax-deductible premiums paid towards your policy. This is in the scenario that nobody in your family is over the age of 60. If you opt for a separate policy for your parents, you can make additional tax savings. In case, neither of your parents is 60 years or older, you can claim a separate deduction of upto INR 25,000 as tax-deductible premiums paid towards the policy each year. Scenario 2- Maximum tax deduction of INR 75,000/year Assuming nobody in your family health policy is over the age of 60, you can claim a tax deduction of INR 25,000 paid towards your health insurance as premiums each year. In a separate policy, you pay the premiums for your parents, at least one of whom is over the age of 60. For this policy, you can claim a separate deduction of upto INR 50,000 annually. Scenario 3- Maximum tax deduction of INR 1,00,000/year In your family floater health plan, if any member is over 60 years old, you can claim a tax deduction on upto INR 50,000 annually paid as health insurance premiums. In the second policy, you have to cover your or your spouse’s parents, you can avail of a separate deduction upto INR 50,000 since one or both parents is over the age of 60.

title: Why a Health Plan of Your Own Matters in Bangalore
content:
Bangalore draws people from across the country, and that shapes how a medical emergency plays out here. The 2011 Census counted about 42.5 lakh workers in Bengaluru Urban district, 44% of its population, and the district is now estimated at around 1.08 crore people. Many of them have moved for work and live far from family, so when a hospital bill arrives, it usually falls on one person's savings.
That risk is growing because the city's health profile is changing. In Karnataka, NFHS-6 (2023-24) found diabetes in 22.3% of women and 26.1% of men, up from 14.0% and 15.6% in NFHS-5. Conditions like these show up in claims: a recent study found that cardiovascular disease and hypertension were the top claim drivers, followed by gastrointestinal conditions and cancer.
The cost of treating them is also climbing. Employer medical costs are projected to rise 11.5% in 2026, while general inflation is 4.1%, so healthcare is getting expensive almost three times as fast as everyday goods. Together, these trends explain why a health plan of your own is one of the most practical financial protections you can have in Bangalore.

title: What Affects Your Premium
content:
Five factors set your premium: age, sum insured, city zone, pre-existing conditions and add-ons. Age is the largest, and the gap between a 25-year-old and a 45-year-old for the same cover can be 3 to 4 times.
- Age: older members cost more.
- Sum insured: higher cover, higher premium.
- City zone: metros such as Bangalore sit in higher-cost zones.
- Pre-existing conditions: a declared condition can add a loading of 10–100%.
- Add-ons: each optional cover adds cost. Multi-year payment can earn a 7–15% discount.
Eligibility Criteria
Adults can generally buy from age 18 with no maximum entry age, and children can be covered from age 16 as dependents. Eligibility also depends on relationship, health disclosure, and KYC.

title: Why West Bengal Health Insurance Become So Important?
content:
The state has seen unprecedented growth in access to healthcare in the last decade. Public-private partnerships, government schemes, and increased awareness have all played their part. But with private hospitals dominating the urban healthcare landscape, costs have become the biggest problem.
A simple three-day hospitalisation due to dengue or viral fever in a good Kolkata hospital can quite easily cost more than INR 75,000 — apart from post-discharge expenses. Think about how hard it would be to foot such an expenditure without insurance in already challenging situations. That's why health insurance in West Bengal is an absolute necessity for families in all income groups.
Also, since people are leading increasingly sedentary lives, lifestyle diseases such as hypertension, diabetes, PCOD, and even premature cardiac conditions have become endemic not only among the elderly but also among young adults. Adding to this the environmental causes of pollution, stress, and diet, it is easy to understand why an insurance safety net is no longer a luxury.

It allows an individual as well as a family floater policyholder to transfer their present health insurance policy, which is indemnity-based, to another insurance firm or even change policies within the same insurance firm.
The main benefit of portability is its continuity factor. While switching insurers, one does not have to begin the mandatory waiting period for pre-existing diseases or specific treatments, as long as the continuity of the insurance history is maintained.

title: Important Factors to Consider Before Porting
content:

- Impact of Age and Medical History: Premium pricing is based on current age and health status. Insurers may apply premium loading if new medical conditions have developed over time.
- Risk of Policy Rejection: Portability is an application process, not an automatic entitlement. Never let an existing policy lapse until the new policy is officially issued and confirmed by the new provider.

title: The Insurance Ombudsman: Meaning
content:
If you have a dispute with your insurance company, the Insurance Ombudsman gives you another way to seek a resolution without immediately going to court. It is an independent, alternate grievance redressal forum set up to help policyholders resolve insurance-related complaints in a cost-effective and impartial manner. The Ombudsman can deal with complaints related to life, health and general insurance, as well as certain group policies and policies issued to sole proprietorships and micro enterprises.
The whole idea is to make the complaint process much simpler and more accessible. The Ombudsman first tries to solve the matter through mediation and makes a fair recommendation based on the facts of the dispute. If the policyholder accepts the recommendation as a full and final settlement, the insurer must comply with it within 15 days. If the matter is not settled through mediation, the Ombudsman can pass a binding award within three months of receiving all the required information from the complainant, and the insurer must comply with the award within 30 days of receiving it.

title: The Complaint Resolution Process
content:
Approaching the Insurance Ombudsman follows a few straightforward steps. Before you approach the Ombudsman, you must first give your insurance company an opportunity to address the issue.
- Initial Complaint: Start by putting your complaint in writing and submitting it directly to your insurance company. This gives the insurer a chance to review the issue and resolve it before you take the matter further.
- Waiting Period: Wait for at least 30 days for your insurer’s response.
- Approaching the Ombudsman: If your insurer does not accept the complaint, gives you an inadequate answer, or simply stays silent for over 30 days, then you are cleared to file with the Insurance Ombudsman.
- Filing the Complaint: Make sure your complaint is in writing and submitted within one year of your insurer’s final decision. Importantly, attach all necessary papers: your policy, correspondence with the insurer, and any claim rejection letter.
Crucially, you cannot contact the Ombudsman if your issue is already being dealt with, or has been resolved, by a court or a consumer forum.

Think of the Insurance Ombudsman as absolutely central to consumer protection within insurance. Its impact is huge, giving policyholders several significant advantages:
- Accessible and Straightforward: This process is kept simple, with no need for complex legal terminology, making it easy for anyone to use.
- Cost-Free: You don’t have to pay a fee to file a complaint with the Insurance Ombudsman. This lets you seek redressal without paying for the legal costs that come with court proceedings.
- Fast Resolution: Complaints are generally dealt with within a few months through the Ombudsman process. Compared with court proceedings, this can offer policyholders a more time-efficient route to resolving an insurance dispute.
- Unbiased Decisions: Being an independent authority means the Ombudsman provides a fair and neutral hearing for everyone involved, both you and the insurer.
The Ombudsman’s mere presence builds immense trust in the insurance world. Policyholders know that there is an external and impartial body they can approach if a dispute arises. A transparent grievance process can give customers greater confidence in insurance. For an insurance agent, knowing the grievance process is useful when a customer has a concern or does not fully understand their policy. A clear explanation and timely intervention can resolve many misunderstandings before they become formal complaints, while also helping the agent earn the customer’s confidence and trust.

title: What Does Health Insurance Claim Rejection Mean?
content:
A health insurance claim rejection means the insurer has decided not to pay the claim, either fully or partially, based on the policy terms and conditions.
This can happen if the treatment is not covered, a waiting period is still applicable, required documents are missing, or certain expenses are not payable. At other times, the insurers don't shut the door in your face but ask for additional documentation. In most cases, when you carefully review their request, you get the inside story regarding what really happened and whether you can still do anything.

title: Why Do You Need an Emigration Clearance?
content:
Before we delve into the "how to" part, it’s worth knowing that the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) initiated this whole emigration clearance process as a safety net. It’s basically a safeguard to make sure nobody takes advantage of you or treats you unfairly while you're working in a foreign country. Sadly, many workers in the past faced harsh conditions or unfair contracts because they didn't have a formal government record of their employment.
The emigration check acts as a safety net. Consider this a security check for your career. It’s there to confirm that your employment contract is legitimate and that your salary is actually fair. While the emigration check ensures your contract is fair, it only provides the most basic medical coverage; therefore, many workers choose to supplement this with a Niva Bupa Travel Insurance policy to ensure they have access to high-quality private healthcare without the burden of massive out-of-pocket expenses.
In simple terms, it is similar to having a supportive figure in the government who reviews your documentation and assures you, "We have thoroughly verified this task for you. It appears secure, the compensation is appropriate, and we are ready to assist you whenever you encounter any difficulties while overseas."

title: ECR vs. Non-ECR: Where Do You Stand?
content:
The first thing you need to do is look at the last page of your passport.
ECR (Emigration Check Required) means that if the person has not finished the standard, also called matriculation, or if the person does not have certificates to prove that the person finished the standard, then the passport will probably carry an ECR stamp.
Non-ECR (formerly ECNR): If you've passed 10th grade, are a taxpayer, or are a graduate, you likely don't need this clearance for most travel.
If your passport is in the ECR category and you are going to one of the 18 specified countries for work, you must apply for an emigration clearance certificate online.

Name-Related Issues: If your contract says "Aman K." but your passport says "Aman Kumar", the POE officer might flag it. Make sure every single letter matches across all documents.
Blurry Photograph: If you’re using your phone to "scan" documents, make sure there’s no glare from the overhead lights. If the officer can't read your visa number clearly, they'll just hit "Reject".
Category Confusion: Are you a "skilled" worker or "unskilled"? If you pick the wrong one, the system might ask for documents you don't have. Double-check your job offer before you select this.
Insurance Dates: Your PBBY insurance needs to start before or on the day you plan to fly and cover your whole contract. If the dates are off by even a day, it’s a red flag.

title: Understanding Emigration Check Required (ECR) Status
content:
Emigration Check Required, or ECR, is a status marked on certain Indian passports. It means the holder needs official clearance before travelling abroad for work. The rule exists to protect workers who might otherwise face exploitation, illegal recruitment, or unsafe conditions in a foreign country.
The clearing process can be considered a safety net. It guarantees that the individual who will be travelling abroad has a valid job offer, a visa, and proper conditions for employment. Although it might seem like one more procedure in an ongoing process, its primary aim is to provide protection for employees.

title: What is an Insurance Claim Procedure?
content:
The insurance claim procedure is the process of filing for a claim with an insurance company to get compensated for a loss. In terms of health insurance, this means informing the insurer about your hospitalisation or treatment, submitting the needed information and documents, and allowing your insurer to assess the claim against the policy terms.
Depending on where you receive treatment and the type of service you use, you may file a cashless claim or a reimbursement claim. Cashless claims are generally processed through Network Health Eco-system, while reimbursement claims involve paying the hospital or healthcare provider first and then submitting the eligible expenses to the insurer for reimbursement.
Understanding the steps to file for a claim in advance can help you know what information to keep ready and where to seek assistance when you need it.

title: How Does the Niva Bupa Claim Process Work?
content: Depending on where you receive treatment, you can either use our cashless facility or pay the hospital yourself and submit a reimbursement claim with us later on. Here's how each process works.
answer_text: Depending on where you receive treatment, you can either use our cashless facility or pay the hospital yourself and submit a reimbursement claim with us later on. Here's how each process works.

title: For Cashless Health Claims
content:
A cashless claim lets us settle approved treatment expenses directly with the hospital, so you don't have to pay the entire eligible hospital bill upfront. You may still need to pay expenses that are not covered under your policy, such as applicable co-payments, deductibles or non-payable items.
For planned hospitalisation, we recommend informing us at least 48 hours before the treatment. In case of emergency hospitalisation, you should intimate us within 24 hours of admission.
Here is how the cashless claim process works:
Step 1: Approach the TPA desk at any one of our Niva Bupa Network Health Eco-system. For planned hospitalisation, we recommend intimating us at least 48 hours before the treatment. In case of emergency hospitalisation, intimate us within 24 hours of admission.
Step 2: Share your Niva Bupa Health Card or policy number with the hospital, along with the required KYC documents and medical records.
Step 3: Now, the Network Health Eco-system will verify your identity for validation and submit the pre-authorisation request to us.
Step 4: After the validation is done, we review and provide our confirmation to the hospital. We ensure you are also notified of the same through SMS and email. We process the initial cashless request within 30 minutes of receiving it from the hospital.
Step 5: Once the treatment is complete, sign the required documents, including the discharge summary and final hospital bill with the detailed breakup.
Step 6: We settle the approved treatment expenses directly with the hospital, as per your policy terms and conditions and the applicable tariff agreed with the hospital. Final approval is processed within 3 hours of receiving the final discharge request.

title: For Reimbursement Health Claim
content:
If you receive treatment at a recognised non-network hospital, you can pay the hospital directly and then submit a reimbursement claim to us for the eligible expenses covered under your policy. You should submit the claim within 30 days from the date of discharge.
Reimbursement claims can be useful when cashless treatment isn't available at the hospital you choose. However, the amount we reimburse depends on your policy's coverage, limits, exclusions and other applicable terms.
Generally, the claim procedure is as follows:
Step 1: Get your treatment at any recognised hospital and settle the hospital bills directly.
Step 2: After you are discharged from the hospital, make sure you have all the relevant documents, invoices, medical reports and discharge certificate with you. We would need the originals of all the mentioned documents to process your reimbursement.
Step 3: Submit your reimbursement claim to us within 30 days from the date of discharge. You can submit the claim through the available online claim submission facility on our website www.nivabupa.com or as per your policy document. A Claim ID is generated within 24 hours of submitting the claim documents.
Step 4: Once we receive your claim documents, we review the claim based on your policy terms and conditions. We may ask for additional information or documents if required.
Step 5: Finally, we will settle the claim (as per policy terms & conditions) and reimburse the approved amount.

title: What is Personal Accident Insurance in India?
content:
Personal accident insurance in India is a specialised policy designed to provide financial protection against injuries, disabilities, or death caused by accidents. Unlike general insurance, it focuses solely on accidental events, offering a lump sum or periodic payments to ease the financial burden. With road accidents claiming over 1.5 lakh lives annually in India, as reported by the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways, the need for such coverage is undeniable.
This insurance is particularly relevant in today’s fast-paced world, where accidents can occur during commutes, travel, or even at home. Our personal accident insurance policies are tailored to meet the diverse needs of Indian families, providing a reliable safety net.

title: Types of Coverage
content:
Personal accident insurance policies offer a range of coverages to address different outcomes of an accident:
Accidental Death: A lump sum is paid to the nominee if the policyholder dies due to an accident.Permanent Total Disability: Covers complete loss of limbs, sight, or other permanent impairments, providing a lump sum to support the policyholder.Permanent Partial Disability: Compensates for partial loss of functionality, such as losing a finger or hearing in one ear.Temporary Total Disability: Offers weekly or monthly payments for temporary inability to work due to an accident.Hospitalisation Expenses: Covers medical costs like surgery, medication, and ambulance charges arising from an accident.Additional Benefits: Some policies include coverage for rehabilitation, childcare, or education funds for dependents.
Our policies are designed to offer comprehensive protection, ensuring all these aspects are covered to meet your needs.

title: What’s Covered Under Individual Personal Accident Insurance?
content:
In India, these policies are designed to provide a comprehensive financial cushion against sudden, unforeseen events. Most standard plans include the following core benefits:
Accidental Death:100% of the Sum Insured is paid to the nominee if the insured person loses their life due to an accident.Permanent Total Disablement (PTD): Payouts for life-altering injuries such as the loss of both eyes or both limbs. Insurers generally pay 100% of the Sum Insured in these cases.Permanent Partial Disablement (PPD): Compensation for the permanent loss of one eye, one limb, or specific fingers, based on a predefined percentage of the Sum Insured.Education Grant: Many Indian policies provide a specific amount for the education of dependent children in the event of the policyholder's death or permanent disability.Transportation of Mortal Remains: Coverage for the costs involved in transporting the body from the site of the accident to the home or cremation ground.Hospital Cash: A daily allowance to manage non-medical expenses during accidental hospitalisation, helping to bridge the gap in incidental costs.

title: What’s Not Covered Under Individual Personal Accident Insurance?
content:
Understanding exclusions is vital to ensure your claim is not rejected. Standard Indian insurance regulations (IRDAI) mandate specific exclusions across the industry:
Self-Inflicted Injury: Any attempt at suicide or deliberate self-harm is strictly excluded.Substance Abuse: Accidents occurring while under the influence of alcohol, drugs, or other intoxicants.Hazardous Activities: Injuries sustained during adventure sports such as paragliding, bungee jumping, or professional motor racing, unless specifically covered by a rider.Breach of Law: Claims arising from the insured person’s participation in illegal acts or criminal activities.War and Nuclear Perils: Injuries resulting from war, invasion, or nuclear radiation.Pre-existing Conditions: Any physical impairment or disability that existed before the policy commencement.

title: Can I cover my children and parents under personal accident policy?
content:
Yes, most Indian insurers offer 'Family Package' or 'Family Floater' options for personal accident cover, allowing for a unified protection plan.
Children: Dependent children can usually be covered from the age of 3 months to 25 years. However, the Sum Insured for children is typically capped at a lower percentage (often 25% to 50%) of the primary insured’s amount.Parents: You can include dependent parents and even parents-in-law in many plans. For senior citizens, the coverage might be restricted to Accidental Death and Permanent Total Disablement, as 'Temporary Total Disablement' benefits are usually reserved for those in active employment.Individual vs. Family Plan: While a health plans for family is cost-effective, high-earning members of the family should ideally have individual covers to ensure the Sum Insured is not spread too thin.

title: How It Differs from Life Insurance and Health Insurance
content:
Personal accident insurance is distinct from life and health insurance, though they complement each other:
Life Insurance: Covers death from any cause, including natural causes, illness, or accidents. It focuses on long-term financial security for dependents but doesn’t cover disability or medical expenses.Health Insurance: Medical insurance plans cover medical expenses for illnesses and accidents but doesn’t provide lump-sum payments for death or disability. It’s broader in scope but may not address income loss.Personal Accident Insurance: Focuses exclusively on accidents, offering lump-sum payments for death or disability and covering accident-related medical costs. It’s more targeted but doesn’t cover non-accidental events.
For comprehensive protection, combining all three is ideal. Our personal accident insurance fills the gap by addressing accident-specific risks.

title: What Is Health Insurance Migration?
content:
Migration is a shift from one product to another within the same insurer. Either you or the insurer can start the process.
Voluntary migration happens when you initiate it, usually because your current plan has restrictive sub-limits or a newer version offers better features, such as unlimited restoration. Compulsory migration happens when the insurer discontinues your product and moves you to a replacement.
In both cases, the benefits you have earned over the years, including waiting periods served, bonuses, and moratorium progress, carry forward within limits.

title: Migration vs. Portability: What is the Difference?
content:
People often confuse migration with portability, but IRDAI clearly separates the two:
Migration: Switching to a different health insurance plan within the same insurance company. You typically need to apply at least 30 days before your renewal date.Portability: Switching your health insurance policy to a completely different insurance company. This process requires fresh underwriting from the new insurer and must be initiated at least 45 to 60 days before your policy expires.
In both cases, IRDAI rules ensure that you do not lose your hard-earned continuity benefits, such as waiting period credits.

title: What is a Critical Illness Insurance Policy?
content:
A critical illness insurance policy is a specialised health insurance product designed to provide financial support upon diagnosis of specific life-threatening or debilitating illnesses. Unlike standard health insurance, which reimburses hospitalisation expenses, critical illness insurance offers a lump-sum payout upon confirmation of a covered condition, regardless of hospitalisation. This payout can be used for medical treatments, recovery aids, debt repayment, or maintaining your lifestyle during recovery.

title: Why Standardisation Matters for Policyholders
content:
Historically, health insurance policy providers used varying definitions for medical exclusions, waiting periods, and policy terms. This lack of uniformity often led to confusion during emergency admissions and claim processing.
IRDAI introduced standardisation guidelines to address these challenges:
- Transparency: The standarised phrasing ensures policy terms mean the same thing across all insurers.
- Consistency: Claim settlement protocols follow uniform regulatory rules regardless of the insurance company.
- Fairness: Arbitrary exclusions based on vague definitions are strictly prohibited.

- Transparency: The standarised phrasing ensures policy terms mean the same thing across all insurers.
- Consistency: Claim settlement protocols follow uniform regulatory rules regardless of the insurance company.
- Fairness: Arbitrary exclusions based on vague definitions are strictly prohibited.

title: Understanding Standardised Exclusions in Health Insurance
content: Health insurance exclusions fall into three distinct categories: standard exclusions, permanent exclusions, and temporary waiting periods.
answer_text: Health insurance exclusions fall into three distinct categories: standard exclusions, permanent exclusions, and temporary waiting periods.

title: 1. Standardisation of Pre-Existing Diseases (PED)
content: According to the regulations by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI), any sickness or disease that was diagnosed or had treatment recommended or taken within 36 months prior to the policy becoming valid is considered a “Pre-existing Disease.” The insurance company cannot rely on any other medical history beyond the 36 months to reject the claim unless there is non-disclosure.
answer_text: According to the regulations by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI), any sickness or disease that was diagnosed or had treatment recommended or taken within 36 months prior to the policy becoming valid is considered a “Pre-existing Disease.” The insurance company cannot rely on any other medical history beyond the 36 months to reject the claim unless there is non-disclosure.

title: 2. Mandatory Inclusion of Modern Advanced Treatments
content:
Health policies can no longer exclude advanced technological procedures. Insurers must provide coverage, either as inpatient care or day-care procedures, for treatments such as:
- Robotic surgeries
- Stem cell therapy
- Oral chemotherapy
- Stereotactic radio surgeries
- Deep brain stimulation
- Intra-vitreal injections
- Vaporisation of the prostate (Green laser (PV) or Holmium laser treatment)

title: 3. Limited Permanent Exclusions
content: IRDAI has defined an exclusive, standardised list of medical conditions that insurers may permanently exclude at the underwriting stage. If an applicant has a condition not included on this regulatory list, insurers cannot apply a permanent exclusion; they must either accept the proposal with standard waiting periods, apply a premium loading, or reject the policy proposal entirely according to board-approved underwriting policies.

title: 4. Standardised Lists of Non-Payable Consumables
content:
Hospital bills frequently contain items categorised as administrative expenses or non-medical consumables. IRDAI has established clear, standardised categories for medical expenses:
- List I: Expenses generally excluded (e.g., administrative fees, toiletries, luxury items)
- List II: Items sub-bound within room charges
- List III: Items sub-bound within procedure charges
- List IV: Items sub-bound within ICU charges
Optional policy add-ons (such as non-medical item covers) allow policyholders to obtain reimbursement for items listed under List I.

title: Exclusions That Remain Standard Across Health Policies
content:
Even though IRDAI has introduced greater consumer protection, certain standard exclusions still remain unless particular riders are added:
- Cosmetic Surgery/Plastic Surgery: Procedures meant for cosmetic purposes only unless the surgery is done for reconstruction after accidents or burns.
- Rest Cure/Rehabilitation: Admission only for rest cure, custodial or sanatorium treatment without any active medical treatment.
- Substance Abuse/Addiction: Inpatient treatment resulting directly from alcoholism, drug abuse, or solvent abuse.
- Breach of Law: Medical expenses incurred by the insured person due to any activity which involves breaking the law.

content: Standard health insurance only pays out if you are admitted for medical treatment. If you stay overnight at a hospital simply for bloodwork, MRI scans, or routine checkups without an underlying condition requiring inpatient care, the entire bill comes out of your pocket unless your policy features an OPD or annual wellness checkup benefit.

title: 2. Why did my hospital bill have random charges that my insurance refused to pay?
content: Those are usually "non-medical expenses" or hospital administrative fees. Things like surgical gloves, PPE kits, admission forms, registration charges, and extra tissues are excluded by default. If you want the insurer to handle these expenses, you will need to add a consumables rider to your plan.

title: 3. Does health insurance cover injuries from playing cricket or riding a scooter?

title: 4. Can I file a claim if my doctor, sibling or uncle treats me at their clinic?
content: Insurance companies strictly exclude treatments provided by immediate family members or doctors who live in the same household, even if they are fully licensed specialists. IRDAI enforces this rule across all insurers to prevent conflicts of interest and inflated billing.

title: 5. Why do standard health insurance policies not cover childbirth?
content: Health plans are meant for unexpected illnesses and accidents. Because pregnancy is a planned medical event, standard policies exclude it unless you specifically pick a family plan with maternity benefits or a maternity rider.

title: What Are Non-Payable Hospital Expenses in Health Insurance?
content:
In simple terms, non-payable expenses are the costs that come up during a hospital stay but aren’t picked up by your insurance provider. Your policy will typically take care of the major costs like room rent, surgery charges, and doctor’s consultations, but there’s a separate category of things used during treatment that fall under “non-medical” items or consumables, and these usually aren’t covered.
The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) has a standardised list of roughly 68 items that are typically excluded from coverage. These generally include items that are for personal comfort, hygiene, or administrative purposes rather than direct medical treatment.

title: Why Is It Important to Check Non-Payable Expenses?
content:
Understanding these expenses before you are hospitalised can save you from significant financial stress. Here is why you should check them:
- Financial Planning: Once you know roughly what your out-of-pocket costs might look like, you can keep a small backup fund ready for whatever the insurer won’t cover.
- Claim Transparency: It also saves you from surprises or disputes with the Third-Party Administrator (TPA) or the insurer when it’s time to actually settle the claim. You can specifically look for one that covers consumables better, or has a rider that fills that gap.

title: What are the Common Types of Non-Payable Hospital Expenses?
content: To better understand your hospital billing breakdown, it is helpful to categorise these non-payable items into four main groups.

title: 1. Administrative and Registration Charges
content:
Hospitals often charge for the administrative work involved in admitting a patient. These include:
- Admission fees
- Discharge procedure charges
- Medical record filing fees
- Birth or death certificate charges

title: 2. Personal Comfort and Hygiene Items
content:
These are items used by the patient for convenience or sanitation but are not considered "medicine." Common examples include:
- Toiletries (Soap, shampoo, combs, toothbrushes)
- Slippers and gowns
- Diapers and sanitary pads
- Water purification packets

title: 3. Non-Medical Consumables
content:
These are "use-and-throw" items required during surgery or recovery. Unless you have a specific "Consumables Cover," these are usually excluded:
- Gloves, masks, and PPE kits
- Nebulisation kits
- Syringes and needles (in some specific basic plans)
- Creams and powders

- Television or Wi-Fi charges
- Laundry services
- Attendant’s meals
- Telephone calls made from the room

content: The most reliable source is your policy wording document. Look for a section titled "Exclusions" or "List of Non-Medical Expenses." Most modern policies include a table or annexure that lists the items the insurer will not pay for.

content:

It can also help policyholders identify expenses that may need to be paid before the final settlement of the hospital bill.

title: How Can You Minimise Out-of-Pocket Hospital Expenses?
content:
You can’t eliminate every non-medical cost, but there are a few practical things you can do to keep them in check.
Choose the Right Room: Try to stay within the room type your policy actually allows for. Stepping up to a pricier room is one of the easiest ways to accidentally trigger proportionate deductions.Carry Your Own Supplies: Hospitals tend to charge more for basics like tissues, sanitiser, and toiletries than you’d pay picking them up yourself beforehand.Ask About Package Rates: Certain procedures, like cataract surgery or knee replacement, sometimes come with all-inclusive hospital packages that already include consumables. Ask about them before you commit to a hospital.Review the Draft Bill: Get the draft bill before discharge and go through it line by line. If something is listed that wasn’t actually used, flag it then and not after you have already signed off the final amount.

title: Can Add-Ons Help Reduce Non-Payable Expenses?
content:
The insurance industry has evolved to address the financial burden of non-payable expenses. Some insurers offer add-ons such as consumables cover to expand the scope of the primary policy.
These riders may cover certain items that are usually classified as non-payable expenses. Depending on the policy, this may include items such as gloves, masks and oxygen masks. Some riders may also offer additional features such as inflation protection or protection of the no-claim bonus, depending on the applicable terms.
Keep in mind that the extra premium and what you actually get for it can differ quite a bit from one add-on to another. So it is worth comparing the benefits and exclusions side by side before you commit to one.

title: Why Women Have Unique Healthcare Needs
content:
Women possess unique healthcare profiles shaped by biological differences, longer average life expectancies, and distinct societal roles.
- Biological Milestones: From menstruation and pregnancy to menopause, women undergo complex hormonal and physiological transitions that require targeted medical supervision, diagnostic screenings, and treatments.
- Longer Life Expectancy: Statistically, women tend to outlive men. This longevity exposes them to a prolonged period of old-age health vulnerabilities, such as osteoporosis and cognitive decline, requiring long-term healthcare financing.
- Disproportionate Risk of Specific Illnesses: Women are more susceptible to certain medical conditions. For instance, autoimmune diseases affect women at a rate nearly two times higher than men.
- The Gender Health Gap: Historically, women tend to deprioritise their health due to familial obligations. A dedicated policy serves as an institutional trigger to encourage regular health check-ups and early medical intervention.

content: Unlike standard indemnity health insurance which reimburses actual hospital expenses, a critical illness plan operates on a benefit-driven model. The policy then concludes, and the policyholder has complete freedom to spend the funds on advanced out-of-network treatments, international travel for care, or daily living expenses.

title: How to Choose the Right Health Insurance Plan for Women
content:
Choosing a health plan requires a clear framework. Use these key pillars to guide your decision:
- Sum Insured: Select a realistic coverage amount. For individuals residing in metropolitan cities, a minimum base cover of INR 10,00,000 is highly recommended to combat rising healthcare inflation.
- Network Hospitals: Verify that major multi-speciality hospitals and local trusted gynaecological clinics near your home are part of the insurer's cashless network.
- Waiting Periods: Review the specific waiting periods required for pre-existing conditions like thyroid imbalances, or specific milestones like maternity care. Opt for plans with shorter waiting periods if you anticipate needing medical services soon.
- Maternity Benefits and Sub-limits: Inspect the precise internal caps placed on maternity claims. Some plans may offer a INR 5,00,000 total sum insured but restrict maternity claims to INR 50,000. Ensure these limits align with current private hospital delivery costs in your city.
- Critical Illness Riders: Check if you can add a critical illness rider directly to your base plan to secure a lump-sum payout for female-centric cancers without needing a separate policy.
- Claim Settlement Support: Examine the insurer's published Claim Settlement Ratio (CSR) and their average speed of settling claims. Consistent, high ratios indicate a reliable, stress-free claims experience.
- Premium Affordability vs Benefits: Do not choose a plan based on a low premium alone. Low-cost policies often include restrictive clauses like high co-payments, room rent caps, or narrow hospital networks. Balance cost with the comprehensive coverage you need.

title: Common Mistakes Women Make When Buying Health Insurance
content:
- Relying Entirely on Corporate Health Insurance: Group health policies provided by employers only last as long as your employment. Furthermore, these corporate policies often feature rigid sub-limits that may not cover complex treatments.
- Concealing Existing Medical Histories: Failing to disclose conditions like PCOS, thyroid issues, or past ovarian cysts when filling out your application can backfire. Insurers investigate medical histories thoroughly during claims, and any non-disclosure can lead to your claim being rejected or your policy being cancelled.
- Ignoring the Specific Sub-limits on Maternity Care: Many buyers look at a large overall policy cover (like INR 10,00,000) and assume all maternity costs are fully covered. In reality, insurers often place strict internal limits (such as a INR 40,000 cap) on childbirth expenses. Always check these specific sub-limits beforehand.
- Delaying the Purchase Until Health Issues Arise: Purchasing insurance after being diagnosed with a chronic disease or finding out you are pregnant is too late. The condition will be classified as a pre-existing disease with a waiting period of up to 4 years, and immediate maternity costs will not be covered.
- Overlooking Fine Print on Exclusions: No health insurance policy covers every single medical expense. Standard plans exclude cosmetic surgeries, experimental treatments, and non-medical items like gloves, gowns, and hygiene products. Reviewing the exclusions list early prevents unexpected financial surprises later.

Insurance firms typically send reminders via email, phone calls, or SMS to ensure you do not miss out on renewing your medical insurance plans. Furthermore, if your policy has expired, you can ask the insurer for a grace period, which normally lasts between 15 and 30 days, and can renew your health insurance online from the convenience of your own home.

Your age largely determines your premium. Experts recommend getting health insurance at a younger age, or at the earliest since it is less when one is younger.
The minimum age for obtaining health insurance for a child is 15 days, and the maximum age is 18.
Adults must be 18 years old to apply, with a maximum age of 65.
The second factor is your overall health. When you get health insurance, you may be required to undergo a medical examination to determine your current health status. This is usually reserved for persons over the age of 45. If you are under the age of 45, you may just be required to submit a doctor's certificate stating that you are in good health.

title: IRDAI Free Look Period Explained: Cancel Your Policy Without Loss
content:
2026-04-23
9 Shares
825 Reads
IRDAI free look period gives policyholders a legally mandated 30-day window to review and cancel a new long-term health or new life insurance policy without major penalties. Running from the exact date you receive your policy documents, this period lets you walk away with a near-full refund (excluding small prorated coverage, stamp duty, and medical fees) if the terms don't match what you were sold.
You bought a health or life insurance policy last week. The agent explained the plan, the brochure looked reassuring, and everything seemed fine. You went ahead and bought it. Then came the policy document, with pages of terms and conditions, including a few things you hadn't discussed with the agent. Now you are wondering whether you made the right call.
The regulator expected exactly this situation, which is why the IRDAI free look period exists. Buying a health insurance policy doesn't mean you have to settle for it without taking a closer look. The free look period gives you time to read the policy, understand the coverage and decide if it works for you. If you change your mind within the applicable period, you can cancel the policy and receive a refund after applicable deductions.

title: What Exactly Is the Free Look Period?
content:
Think of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) free look period as a cooling-off window. It is the time between receiving your policy document and being formally committed to it. During this period, you can thoroughly read every page, compare the actual policy terms against what the agent told you, and then decide if this is genuinely what you wanted to buy.
This concept exists because insurance is not like buying clothes. It is a financial commitment you are making, sometimes for decades. And that, too, is based on a product that is complex and often explained quickly during a sales conversation. Mis-selling is a significant and common problem in the insurance industry, which can be resolved with the concept of a free look period, which IRDAI has created specifically to address it.

title: How Long Is the Window and When Does It Start?
content:
You get 30 days to review your health insurance policy under Section 20 of the IRDAI Regulations 2024. This free look period applies whether you bought the policy directly from the insurer, through an agent, or online.
Applicability: The 30‑day free look period is the same for all policies with a term of one year or more covering individual health or new life insurance plans. Short‑term policies that last under one year are usually not covered by the 30‑day free look period.The Starting Trigger: The 30‑day free look period clock begins on the day you actually receive the policy document, not on the purchase date or the policy start date.Delivery Proof: For policies, the 30‑day free look period starts from the email timestamp. For copies, it begins from the courier or postal delivery confirmation.
Remark: Prior to the introduction of the 2024 revision, the period during which one could consider the policy was just 15 days for all offline policies. The 30-day free look period provides ample time to discuss your options with a counselor or relative.

title: What Happens If You Miss the 30-Day Window?
content:
Missing the window makes exiting much harder:
- Health Insurance Exits: You will not get a full refund mid-term, but at your next renewal, you can utilise policy portability to transfer your cover to another insurer without losing accumulated waiting period benefits.
- Grievances and Mis-Selling: If you believe your policy was sold to you unfairly and you have the evidence to back it up, raise the matter with your insurer first. And if you still don't hear back or receive a satisfactory resolution within 30 days, you can then approach the Insurance Ombudsman.

content:
IRDAI regulates India's insurance sector. It decides:
- How insurance policies are structured.
- How premiums are set.
- How claims get processed and settled.
Since every insurer has to comply, a rule change at the IRDAI level eventually shows up in your policy document, your claim experience, or your renewal notice.

IRDAI regulates India's insurance sector. It decides:
- How insurance policies are structured.

- How claims get processed and settled.
Since every insurer has to comply, a rule change at the IRDAI level eventually shows up in your policy document, your claim experience, or your renewal notice.

title: No Age Limit on Buying Health Insurance
content:
Age is no longer a barrier to buying a policy.
- Earlier, insurers set upper age limits, often 60 or 65 years.
- People above that age struggled to find coverage at all.
- This restriction has now been removed completely, opening the market to senior citizens who were previously locked out.

title: Reduced Waiting Periods
content:
Waiting periods have come down across the board.
- The waiting period for pre-existing conditions has been cut from 4 years to 3 years.
- Knee replacement surgeries, previously left to each insurer's discretion with no fixed cap, are now capped at 3 years too.
- Once the 3-year mark passes, all policyholders become eligible to claim for both.
This is important for individuals with chronic conditions like diabetes or hypertension. People with such conditions have usually had to wait for years before the costs of their treatment were even covered.

title: Mandatory Coverage for Severe Illnesses
content:
Insurers can no longer turn away serious cases.
- Cancer, stroke, renal failure, and AIDS previously could be excluded at an insurer's discretion.
- All health insurance providers must now cover these conditions.
- This removes a major gap for policyholders without the financial cushion to self-fund treatment for a critical illness.

title: AYUSH Treatments Covered Up to Full Sum Insured
content:
AYUSH treatment, covering Ayurveda, Yoga, Unani, Siddha, and Homoeopathy, gets the same treatment as conventional medicine now.
- Sub-limits on AYUSH claims have been removed.
- Policyholders can claim up to their full sum insured, same as any other procedure.
- This benefits patients who rely on alternative treatment systems alongside or instead of allopathic care.

title: Moratorium Period Capped at 5 Years
content:
The moratorium period is the point after which an insurer loses the right to reject a claim over non-disclosure, unless fraud is involved.
- Previously, this period varied by insurer, often stretching well past 5 years.
- It is now capped at 5 years (60 months) of continuous coverage.
- Once a policy crosses this mark, claims cannot be denied on disclosure grounds, giving long-term policyholders far more certainty.

title: Introduction of Benefit-Based Policies
content:
A new policy type has entered the market.
- Benefit‑based plans pay a fixed lump sum on diagnosis and can be stacked with other policies.
- Indemnity plans reimburse actual expenses and are subject to the principle of indemnity.
- Works well alongside an indemnity plan for added financial cushion during treatment.

title: Telemedicine Included in Coverage
content:
Online consultations are now typically a covered expense. It still depends on the policy type.
- Telemedicine usage grew sharply during the pandemic, but costs often fell outside policy coverage.
- IRDAI has pushed for more insurers to cover telemedicine.
- Consultations done online can now be claimed the same way an in-person visit would be.

title: Cashless Claims to Be Approved Within 3 Hours
content:
Approval delays now have a hard deadline.
- Earlier, there was no fixed timeline, and approvals sometimes dragged on for days.
- Insurers must now approve or reject cashless claims within 3 hours of receiving discharge papers.
- This directly reduces the time patients spend waiting to leave a hospital after treatment.

title: Multiple Claims Allowed Across Insurers
content:
Benefit-based policyholders get more flexibility.
- If you hold a benefit-based plan, you can file claims with multiple insurers for the same illness.
- This is different from indemnity plans, where reimbursement is capped at actual expenses.
- Useful during a major health crisis where costs from one payout alone may not cover everything.

title: Network Hospital Transparency
content:
Finding the right hospital should get easier.
- Insurers were not previously required to maintain or share updated network hospital lists.
- This is now mandatory, along with clear reimbursement guidelines for treatment taken outside the network.
- It's worth checking this list before buying a policy, especially if you have a preferred hospital nearby.

content:

- IRDAI has capped hikes at 10% without prior regulatory approval.
- Anything beyond that requires the insurer to justify the increase to IRDAI first.

title: Grace period for premium payment
content: Life insurance policies carry a grace period of 30 days from the premium due date. The policy stays in force during the grace period. If the premium is unpaid when the grace period ends, the policy lapses.
answer_text: May 30 days po kayong grace period from the due date. Active pa rin po ang policy ninyo within that period. Pag lumagpas po, saka lang mag-la-lapse.

title: What happens when a policy lapses
content: A lapsed policy no longer provides coverage. Claims filed while the policy is lapsed are not payable. The policy may be reinstated within a set period by paying overdue premiums, sometimes with evidence of insurability.
answer_text: Pag na-lapse po, wala na pong coverage, at hindi po mababayaran ang claims. Pwede pa po i-reinstate within a certain period — babayaran lang po ang overdue premiums.

title: Reinstatement of a lapsed policy
content: Reinstatement is generally allowed within two to three years of lapse. It requires payment of all overdue premiums with interest, and the insurer may require updated health declarations.
answer_text: Pwede po i-reinstate within two to three years ng lapse. Kailangan lang po bayaran lahat ng overdue premiums, at minsan may health declaration po ulit.

title: Changing a beneficiary
content: A policyholder may change a revocable beneficiary at any time by submitting a change-of-beneficiary form. An irrevocable beneficiary cannot be changed without that beneficiary's written consent.
answer_text: Pwede po ninyong palitan ang beneficiary anytime kung revocable — may form lang po. Pero kung irrevocable po, kailangan po ng consent ng beneficiary mismo.

title: What a rider adds to a policy
content: A rider is an add-on benefit attached to a base life policy, such as critical illness, accidental death, or waiver of premium. Riders increase the total premium and have their own terms.
answer_text: Ang rider po ay add-on sa base policy ninyo — tulad po ng critical illness, accidental death, o waiver of premium. May dagdag po siya sa premium, at may sarili pong terms.

title: Waiver of premium rider
content: A waiver of premium rider keeps the policy in force without further premium payments if the insured becomes totally and permanently disabled, subject to the rider's definitions and waiting period.
answer_text: Kung may waiver of premium rider po kayo, tuloy pa rin po ang policy kahit hindi na kayo makapagbayad, kung ma-totally and permanently disabled po kayo — depende po sa terms ng rider.

title: Filing a death claim
content: A death claim requires the original policy contract, a certified death certificate, claimant identification, and a completed claim form. Processing typically begins once documents are complete.
answer_text: Para po sa death claim, kailangan po ang original policy, certified death certificate, valid ID ng claimant, at claim form. Magsisimula po ang processing pag kumpleto na po lahat.

title: Contestability period
content: Most life policies have a two-year contestability period from issue or reinstatement. Within this period the insurer may contest a claim on grounds of material misrepresentation in the application.
answer_text: May two-year contestability period po ang karamihan ng policies. Within po ng period na yan, pwede pong i-contest ang claim kung may maling na-declare sa application.

title: Premium payment channels
content: Premiums may be paid through the partner bank over the counter, via online banking, through auto-debit arrangement, or at accredited payment centres. Auto-debit reduces the risk of accidental lapse.
answer_text: Pwede po kayong magbayad sa bangko over the counter, online banking, auto-debit, o sa mga payment centers. Mas safe po ang auto-debit para hindi po kayo ma-lapse.

title: Value of coverage versus cost
content: Life insurance transfers the financial impact of an untimely death from the family to the insurer. The benefit is paid as a lump sum to beneficiaries and is generally not subject to the delays of estate settlement.
answer_text: Naiintindihan ko po na gastos siya monthly. Pero ang life insurance po kasi, siya ang sasalo sa pamilya ninyo kung may mangyari. Direkta po sa beneficiary ang proceeds, hindi po kailangang maghintay ng estate settlement.

title: Already covered by employer insurance
content: Employer-provided group life cover usually ends when employment ends and is typically a multiple of salary rather than a needs-based amount. A personal policy stays with the policyholder across jobs.
answer_text: Okay po yan, pero yung group life po sa trabaho, natatapos po pag nag-resign o nag-transfer kayo. Yung personal policy po, sa inyo po talaga yan kahit magpalit kayo ng trabaho.

title: Policy loan availability
content: Policies with accumulated cash value may allow a policy loan. The loan accrues interest and any unpaid balance is deducted from the death benefit or surrender value.
answer_text: Kung may cash value na po ang policy ninyo, pwede po kayong mag-policy loan. May interest lang po, at mababawas po sa benefit kung hindi mabayaran.

title: Late payment penalty
content: A late fee is charged per day of delay on an overdue instalment, calculated as a percentage of the outstanding instalment amount. The exact rate is stated in the financing agreement.
answer_text: Untuk keterlambatan, ada denda harian ya Pak, dihitung dari nilai angsuran yang tertunggak. Nominal persisnya tercantum di perjanjian pembiayaan Bapak.

title: Instalment due date and grace
content: The instalment due date is fixed each month per the financing agreement. Payment received after the due date is treated as late and incurs a penalty from the first day of delay.
answer_text: Jatuh tempo cicilan Bapak tetap setiap bulan sesuai perjanjian. Kalau pembayaran masuk setelah tanggal itu, dihitung telat dan kena denda mulai hari pertama ya.

title: Payment relief and restructuring
content: Customers experiencing documented financial hardship may apply for relief, which can include rescheduling the tenor or temporarily reducing the instalment. Approval requires assessment and supporting documents; it is not automatic.
answer_text: Kalau memang kondisinya sedang berat, Bapak bisa mengajukan keringanan — bisa perpanjangan tenor atau penyesuaian angsuran sementara. Tapi perlu diajukan dan dinilai dulu ya Pak, tidak otomatis disetujui.

title: How to apply for relief
content: A relief application is submitted through customer service with proof of the hardship, such as a termination letter or medical records. The assessment outcome is communicated in writing.
answer_text: Pengajuan keringanan lewat customer service ya Pak, dengan bukti pendukung seperti surat PHK atau dokumen medis. Nanti hasilnya diinformasikan tertulis.

title: Early settlement
content: A customer may settle the remaining balance early. An early settlement fee may apply, and the payoff amount must be requested from customer service as it changes daily.
answer_text: Bisa Pak, pelunasan dipercepat diperbolehkan. Biasanya ada biaya pelunasan dipercepat, dan nominalnya harus diminta ke customer service karena berubah tiap hari.

title: Payment channels
content: Instalments can be paid by bank transfer to a virtual account, through partner minimarkets, via mobile banking, or by auto-debit. Virtual account transfers are credited fastest.
answer_text: Pembayaran bisa lewat transfer ke virtual account, minimarket, mobile banking, atau auto-debit Pak. Paling cepat masuk itu transfer ke virtual account.

title: Payment not yet reflected
content: A payment may take one to two business days to reflect, depending on the channel used. Customers should keep the transfer receipt and report it to customer service if it has not appeared.
answer_text: Kadang pembayaran butuh satu sampai dua hari kerja untuk masuk, tergantung channel-nya Pak. Mohon simpan bukti transfernya, nanti bisa dilaporkan ke customer service kalau belum muncul.

title: Tenor and instalment relationship
content: A longer tenor lowers the monthly instalment but increases the total amount paid over the financing period. A shorter tenor raises the monthly instalment and lowers the total cost.
answer_text: Kalau tenornya lebih panjang, cicilan bulanannya lebih ringan, tapi total yang dibayar jadi lebih besar. Kalau tenor pendek, cicilan lebih besar tapi totalnya lebih hemat.

title: Down payment requirement
content: A down payment is required at the start of financing. The percentage depends on the asset type and the customer's credit assessment.
answer_text: DP memang disyaratkan di awal pembiayaan Pak. Besarannya tergantung jenis unit dan hasil penilaian kredit Bapak.

title: Documents held during financing
content: The ownership document is held by the financing company until the financing is fully settled. It is released to the customer after final payment and administrative processing.
answer_text: Dokumen kepemilikan disimpan perusahaan pembiayaan sampai lunas ya Pak. Setelah pelunasan dan proses administrasi selesai, baru diserahkan ke Bapak.

title: Dispute over penalty amount
content: Late fees accrue daily from the first day after the due date, so a penalty can grow larger than expected if several instalments are missed. The calculation basis is set out in the financing agreement.
answer_text: Dendanya dihitung harian dari hari pertama setelah jatuh tempo Pak, jadi kalau beberapa bulan tertunggak memang bisa terasa besar. Cara hitungnya ada di perjanjian pembiayaan.

title: Updating contact details
content: Customers should update their phone number and address with customer service so that payment reminders and statements are received on time.
answer_text: Kalau nomor atau alamat Bapak berubah, mohon diinfokan ke customer service ya, supaya reminder dan tagihan tetap sampai tepat waktu.

content:
2.1.7. Co-payment means a cost-sharing requirement under a health insurance policy that provides that the Policyholder/insured
will bear a specified percentage of the admissible claim amount. A Co-payment does not reduce the Sum Insured.
2.1.8. Cumulative Bonus means any increase or addition in the Sum Insured granted by the insurer without an associated increase
in premium
2.1.9. Day Care Centre means any institution established for Day Care Treatment of Illness and/or Injuries or a medical set-up with
a Hospital and which has been registered with the local authorities, wherever applicable, and is under the supervision of a
registered and qualified Medical Practitioner AND must comply with all minimum criterion as under:
a. has Qualified Nursing staff under its employment;
b. has qualified Medical Practitioner(s) in charge;
c. has a fully equipped operation theatre of its own where Surgical Procedures are carried out;
d. maintains daily records of patients and will make these accessible to the insurance company’s authorized personnel.
2.1.10. Day Care Treatment refers to medical treatment, and/or Surgical Procedure which is:
a. undertaken under General or Local Anaesthesia in a Hospital/Day Care Centre in less than 24 hrs because of technological
advancement, and
b. which would have otherwise required a Hospitalization of more than 24 hours. Treatment normally taken on an out patient basis is not included in the scope of this definition.
2.1.11. Dental Treatment means a treatment related to teeth or structures supporting teeth including examinations, fillings (where
appropriate), crowns, extractions and Surgery.
2.1.12. Deductible means a cost-sharing requirement under a health insurance policy that provides that the Insurer will not be liable

title: ReAssure 2.0: Year 2: Once the policy is renewed
content:
At the time of renewal (in case of a claim), the premium will be charged as per the current age of the consumer at renewal.
•
If you add a member to the floater plan, then the premiums will be charged as per the entry age of the eldest member and will
lock the premium at that age, till a claim is paid.
•
If you add a member to an individual plan and convert it into a Floater plan, then the premiums will be charged as per the entry
age of the eldest member and will lock the premium at that age, till a claim is paid.
•
If the eldest member is no longer part of the Floater plan, then the Floater premium will be calculated as per the original entry age
of the eldest member in the policy amongst the remaining members and lock at that age, till a claim is paid.
•
If a floater plan, splits into multiple policies, then we will carry forward the locked age at which the floater policies were taken by
individuals (as per the claim history) in the policies carried forward, till a claim is paid.
•
In a multi individual policy, the age will unlock only for the individuals who claim.
•
In a floater policy, if a claim is paid for anyone in the plan then we will unlock the age for the entire policy.
•
We will consider a claim, if a claim is paid under the following: Expenses in reaching a Hospital, Expenses during Hospitalization,
Expenses before and after hospitalization, Home Care / Domiciliary Treatment, Organ Donor.

provided that the Policy is renewed without break.

4.11. Shared accommodation Cash Benefit
If you opt for a shared room (for which hospitalization claim is paid), we will pay an additional amount for each day’s hospitalization. One day is considered as 24 continuous hours of hospitalization.
4.12. Second Medical Opinion
Once in a Policy year, you can choose to take a second medical opinion from any Medical Practitioner for which we have paid a claim
under expenses during hospitalization.. Through our partners we can help you get a second opinion from some of the most reputed
doctors in the country.
4.13. e-Consultation
You can take Unlimited e-consultations from our Partners. Optional Benefit:
4.14. Hospital Cash
We will pay for an Insured, an additional fixed amount for each day’s hospitalization for maximum up to 30 days. One day is considered
as 24 continuous hours of hospitalization. Note: we will pay if you were hospitalized for 48 hours or more continuously.
